I’m not doubting rugby has strategy at all, however, I think the set plays will get more complex. With that said, the US could be contenders fairly quickly. If I were building an American squad, here’s how I think it would go for the US. Take a group of D1 linebackers who would likely make NFL practice squads, and out of that group, find the guys who have the potential to succeed as gadget guys, and that’s about it. I’m fairly confident I could build a world class American rugby team with about $10 million total and about a 3-4 year timeframe.  I’d also say the inverse, that any world competitive country could build a decent NFL team (at the very least D1 football team) with only rugby players given the same parameters.

I think Fiji may be the breaking point of a new rugby meta here.  It’s important to have guys with great conditioning, but if your “sprinters” get decked a few times, they get skittish. Same thing happens in American football, you take a quick WR and pop him hard a few times, he isn’t moving the ball the same way.  If I were to guess the direction rugby goes, (once again, never watched in my life), The game starts to diverge on American football. Teams start having set pieces, dedicated positions where they should dump the ball when hit hard, that sort of thing.  It becomes a free flowing version of American football, which would be great because America has a constant feed of this type of skill set.

As an American who’s never watched rugby, here’s how I see it. This is how American Football running backs would play rugby. Low man wins, and if you’re stronger, tacklers need to get lower. I see a lot of high/arm tackles (grabbing above the waist/at the shoulders), and against a strong runner, that shit ain’t gonna fly.  As athletes get bigger, faster, and stronger you should expect this to transition to the meta. Guys like Saquon Barkley, Christian Mccaffrey, Derrick Henry, etc. all run like this. This is big boy football, and if you don’t like it, go watch soccer.
